title: core/map.odin header documents a district-scoped ATTACH draw that contradicts the shipped global-ring implementation
detail: The code does the opposite: growth.odin:532 states 'The ring is GLOBAL (not district-scoped)' and growth_board_ring_scan loops `for k in 0..<len(board.candidates)` with no district filter. Spec scope 3 requires 'document the exact interplay' — two shipped docs describe contradictory interplays; map.odin describes behavior that does not exist.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the map.odin paragraph to document the shipped global street ring (with the measured 63%-district-starvation rationale from the PR), or implement the district-scoped draw it claims.

title: demos/dublin_board.dem header repeats the false district-scoped ATTACH claim in the named golden's docs
evidence:
# growth spawns land on the board's real-street tile pool (the 1-in-6 density,
# the user's blessed calm default) with estates clustering within districts
# (the growth_groups interplay: the ATTACH family draws from the anchor's
# district pool — a cluster never crosses a district boundary).
detail: Same contradiction as core/map.odin: growth_board_ring_scan draws from the global pool (growth.odin:537-549), so an estate CAN cross district Voronoi boundaries. The golden's authoritative header documents unimplemented behavior.
recommended_fix: Update the .dem header to describe the global street ring actually blessed by this golden.

title: map_test.odin header claims district pins (b)/(d) that no test asserts; district pool data is dead in the sim
detail: No test asserts loader district assignment, district_start ranges, or within-district attaches (test_growth_dublin_attach_stays_in_estate_radius checks pool membership + radius only). candidate_district/district_start are never read by the sim — only built by the test helper.
recommended_fix: Either add assertions for (b)/(d) or restate the header to the shipped global-ring behavior; if district data stays unused, note it is reserved for a future policy.

title: map_board_load error paths after partial allocation leak the partially-built board (ODN-18 arena discipline)
evidence:
p, okp := map_json_f32_pair(cands[i])
		if !okp {
			return {}, "map_board_load: malformed spawn candidate"
--- (allocations already made into b before this return) ---
286:		b.attribution = strings_clone(attr, allocator)
319:		append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = strings_clone(name, allocator), kind = kind, pos = {f32(px), f32(py)}})
detail: Every `return {}, err` after the attribution/district/candidate allocations (e.g. lines 335, 380, and the terrain/streets errors) discards the named `b`, orphaning its cloned strings and dynamic arrays — a leak the project's tracking-allocator rule ('leaks are CI failures') forbids.
recommended_fix: Return the partial `b` alongside the error and have callers map_board_destroy it, or free b's buffers via defer-on-error before each late failure return.

title: map_board_destroy's stated contract 'the app frees at exit' is false — no caller in app/ or harness/ ever frees the board
detail: grep across app/ and harness/ finds map_board_destroy referenced only in core/map.odin (definition) and core/map_test.odin. app/main.odin:429 stores the board (context.allocator) with no teardown, unlike catalogs which get `defer pp.catalogs_destroy` (main.odin:276).
recommended_fix: Add a map_board_destroy call at app exit (near the drop_marks/drop_reasons cleanup), or correct the comment to say the board intentionally lives for the process.

title: T1 hash carries only the 1-byte map id — the dublin.json asset bytes that drive every dublin spawn have no content hash
detail: Spec scope 2: 'the map is part of the run state, hashed like a seed'. Catalogs — the other caller-loaded sim data — get catalog_hash; a re-baked dublin.json (same dims) changes all dublin spawns with no manifest-level pin distinguishing asset drift from code drift.
recommended_fix: Hash the board asset bytes at load (e.g. FNV-64 over dublin.json) onto Map_Board and fold it into the T1 state hash next to map_source, mirroring catalog_hash.
